nodes.description: Cbl-b is upregulated in T cells by tolerising signals and is required for anergy induction, so without it self-reactive T cells that should be silenced in the periphery remain able to respond. Mice lacking it fail to induce T-cell tolerance in vitro and in vivo, develop spontaneous autoimmunity with autoantibodies and lymphocytic infiltration of multiple organs, and are strikingly susceptible to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis. This is the step at which a cell-intrinsic signalling abnormality becomes an autoimmune disease, and it is also the weakest step in the human chain: the patients' tolerance was never assayed directly, and the knock-in mouse that reproduces their cellular phenotype does not develop autoimmune disease in clean housing.

nodes.description: A clean genetic separation of the two ways the human variants are loss of function: it preserves the protein but abolishes only its E3 ligase activity, and still phenocopies the null. It is the animal result that licenses grading a CBLB allele with preserved protein expression, such as the third family's p.C464W, as loss of function rather than requiring absent protein.

The original gene-targeted null, and the animal counterpart of the human disease rather than of a particular allele. It develops spontaneous autoimmunity with autoantibody production, infiltration of activated T and B lymphocytes into multiple organs and parenchymal damage; its resting lymphocytes hyperproliferate on antigen receptor stimulation, its T cells overproduce interleukin-2 specifically, and T-cell proliferation, interleukin-2 production and Vav1 phosphorylation are uncoupled from the requirement for CD28 costimulation. It fails to induce T-cell tolerance in vitro and in vivo, is strikingly susceptible to experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, and its effector T cells resist regulatory T cells in vivo including when genuinely naive, while its regulatory T cells function normally. Whether it develops autoimmunity is not fully reproducible: of the two independently generated null lines, autoantibodies and spontaneous disease were found in one and not the other.

nodes.description: CRISPR/Cas9 knock-in of the mouse residue corresponding to the first patient's p.H285L, generated to test whether that allele predisposes to immune dysregulation. It reproduces the expression defect, at about half wild-type protein, and the cellular phenotype: effector T cell hyperproliferation with increased interleukin-2 and no further gain from anti-CD28, resistance of those effector cells to wild-type regulatory T cells, increased and prolonged B-cell SYK phosphorylation with hyperproliferation after IgM cross-linking, hyperactivated bone-marrow-derived mast cells, and exaggerated IgE-mediated passive anaphylaxis. What it does not reproduce is the disease. At one year the mice were healthy, without lymphadenopathy or organomegaly, with no cellular infiltrate in salivary gland, liver or kidney and HEp-2-reactive autoantibody titres no different from wild type. Two findings also run against the patient: splenic regulatory T cells are increased where the patient's were decreased, and the B-cell signalling gain produced no increase in germinal-centre B cells or antibody.

nodes.description: A naturally occurring Cblb-mutant animal disease rather than an engineered model. Positional cloning of the KDP rat's major non-MHC type 1 diabetes locus, Iddm/kdp1, identified a nonsense mutation in Cblb, and the strain's diabetes is accounted for by that gene together with the MHC haplotype. It is the closest animal counterpart of this disease's organ pattern: moved onto an MHC class II 'a' background, Cblb-homozygous congenic rats develop autoimmune thyroiditis without diabetes, and on the original 'u' background they develop diabetes. So the same lesion gives thyroid or islet autoimmunity depending on the MHC haplotype, while the patients have both. Those congenics also show alopecia, which the patients do not, and the thyroiditis occurred without clinical hypothyroidism, which the patients have.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a major gene responsible for type 1 diabetes in the Komeda diabetes-prone rat.
evidence.snippet: we identified a nonsense mutation in the Casitas B-lineage lymphoma b (Cblb) gene by positional cloning of Iddm/kdp1

nodes.description: CBL-B is a negative regulator of antigen receptor signalling, and its expression in T cells is itself controlled by signals downstream of the T-cell receptor and CD28. Without it, receptor-proximal signalling proteins escape ubiquitin-dependent degradation. The affected step is selective rather than global: in Cbl-b-null T cells the main T-cell receptor pathways, Zap-70 and Lck, the Ras/MAP kinase cascade, phospholipase C-gamma-1 and calcium mobilisation, are unaffected, while Vav activation is enhanced; and in the knock-in mouse carrying the patient allele, LAT and PLC-gamma-1 phosphorylation, calcium flux, and ERK1/2 and AKT phosphorylation after anti-CD3 stimulation are all normal despite the hyperproliferation. In B cells the picture is the opposite: BCR ligation produces increased and prolonged SYK phosphorylation.
nodes.id: Loss of CBL-B Restraint on Antigen Receptor Signalling

biological_processes: negative regulation of T cell receptor signaling by CBL-B

evidence.reference_title: Cbl-b regulates the CD28 dependence of T-cell activation.

In contrast, the activation of Vav, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor for Rac1/Rho/CDC42, was significantly enhanced.

nodes.description: The arm behind the urticarial phenotype. Bone-marrow-derived mast cells from the knock-in mouse have increased and sustained SYK, PLC-gamma-1 and PLC-gamma-2 phosphorylation after Fc-epsilon receptor cross-linking, more surface LAMP-1 mobilisation, and the animals have exaggerated IgE-dependent passive anaphylaxis with higher mast cell protease 1. In the patient the corresponding observation is indirect: her plasma, unlike control plasma, strongly activated normal basophils, and she had no detectable IgE to environmental allergens and no atopic history, so the urticaria is attributed to a serum activating factor rather than to allergy.

animal_models.description: The only arm where the model goes all the way to a whole-animal outcome: Fc-epsilon-receptor-proximal hyperphosphorylation and LAMP-1 mobilisation in cultured mast cells, and exaggerated IgE-mediated passive anaphylaxis with raised mast cell protease 1 in the animal.

nodes.description: The disease's effector output. Two of the three children had broad autoantibody panels run and both showed many raised specificities: IgG against 19 autoantigens in one, including insulin and GAD65, and against 14 in the other, insulin among them. No plasma was available from the third. The organ-level consequences downstream of this node are what the children presented with, and they differ between them, so the node is deliberately a multi-organ one rather than an organ-specific lesion.

nodes.description: An inflammatory, non-organ-specific arm that dominated one child's presentation and was detectable in another. Plasma interleukin-6, tumour necrosis factor alpha, interleukin-10, CXCL9 and CXCL10 were substantially raised in the first patient and interleukin-6, tumour necrosis factor alpha, CXCL9 and CXCL10 in the third. The second child presented at three years with fevers, lung infiltrates, hepatomegaly and ascites, and later with fevers and arthralgia and marrow hemophagocytosis, having been screened negative for familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis genes and for an infectious trigger. His cytokine levels were only modestly raised, which the authors attribute to his being asymptomatic when sampled.

nodes.description: The one functional abnormality demonstrated in more than one patient. CD4+ T cells from the patient with p.H285L and from the patient with p.R496X both hyperproliferated on anti-CD3 stimulation relative to controls. In the knock-in mouse the same cells also secrete more interleukin-2 and, unlike wild-type T cells, gain nothing further from added anti-CD28, so the costimulation requirement is already satisfied. Human patient cells did show a further increase with anti-CD28, so the mouse's complete uncoupling is not reproduced in the patients.
nodes.id: T Cell Hyperproliferation Uncoupled from CD28 Costimulation
